Send the complete list at quotation and the conformity work runs in parallel with picking. Where a line falls outside the regulated scope we say so rather than charge for paperwork nobody needs.

faqs.q: Why does road freight to Bahrain take longer than to Dammam?
faqs.a: Because it transits Saudi Arabia and then crosses the King Fahd Causeway. The consignment carries Saudi transit formalities as well as Bahraini import ones, and the causeway adds a queue that nobody can promise to the hour. Road freight is typically three to four working days from dispatch, routed via Al Batha and Dammam; air into Bahrain International removes both the transit leg and the queue.

faqs.q: Can you deliver to Hidd and the Bahrain Logistics Zone?
faqs.a: Yes, on DAP terms to the gate. Both sit inside the Manama–Muharraq belt and add no meaningful time to the inland leg after the causeway. The same applies to Sitra, Askar and Salman Industrial City. Send the consignee and site contact details with the order so the final delivery is booked against the right gate.

faqs.q: Which lines need a GCC Conformity Mark for Bahrain?
faqs.a: Only the regulated categories. At quotation we go through your list and state which lines fall inside the regulated scope and which do not, so the mark is applied where it is required and nowhere else. The requirement is the same whether the consignment crosses the King Fahd Causeway or flies into Bahrain International.

faqs.q: Can you supply to smelter and refinery specifications?
faqs.a: Yes. Where a specification names a standard — ISO 18752, EN 856 4SP, NACE MR0175 — we quote against that standard and the certification travels with the goods. For valve and flow-iron lines, API 6A and API 16C are quoted the same way. Send the specification sheet or the end user's datasheet with the enquiry, so the quote is built against it rather than corrected afterwards.

faqs.q: What documents travel with a road consignment to Bahrain?
faqs.a: An attested Dubai Chamber Certificate of Origin, the commercial invoice and packing list, Saudi transit documents for the road leg arranged by the nominated road carrier, a GCC Conformity Mark for regulated lines, and material and test certificates where the order calls for them. Air freight into Bahrain International removes the Saudi transit leg but not the rest of the set. All of it is prepared before dispatch.

faqs.q: When is air freight to Bahrain worth it?
faqs.a: When the schedule matters more than the freight cost. Air from Dubai to Bahrain International takes one to two days and removes both the Saudi transit leg and the causeway queue, which is the one part of the road lane nobody can promise to the hour. For a line that is down at a smelter or refinery that usually decides it; for planned maintenance, road at three to four working days is cheaper.

faqs.q: Can you supply fittings that are hard to find in Bahrain?
faqs.a: Yes, and that is where buying from Dubai helps most. GOST couplings, exotic-alloy metallic hose, food-grade lubricants and ORFS adapters in sizes nobody stocks locally are ordinary line items on our catalogue rather than special imports. They travel on the same consignment as the everyday hose and fittings instead of being chased separately weeks later.

faqs.q: Can you make hose assemblies to length for Sitra or Askar?
faqs.a: Yes. Assemblies are crimped and pressure-tested in Dubai and shipped finished, each tagged with the hose, the fitting and the test date. For smelter and refinery service send the hose standard — ISO 18752, EN 856 4SP or the SAE J517 equivalent — with both end fittings and the overall length, and we build to it. An old tag or sample works where the part number is lost.

faqs.q: Do you supply lifting gear to Bahrain?
faqs.a: Yes. Slings, shackles and rigging hardware ship marked with their working load limit and with the manufacturer's test certificates the order calls for, on the same consignment as hydraulic parts. Whether a lifting line falls inside the regulated scope is confirmed at quotation. Inspection on site stays with your appointed lifting inspector; send the certificate format they require and we confirm the document set.

faqs.q: Can you ship by sea to Khalifa Bin Salman Port?
faqs.a: Yes. LCL from Jebel Ali to Khalifa Bin Salman Port takes six to nine days and suits heavy or oversize packages that would be awkward on a truck across the causeway. CIF Khalifa Bin Salman Port is one of the Incoterms we quote, alongside DAP to your site, FOB Jebel Ali and EXW Dubai for a nominated forwarder.

faqs.q: How do I request a quote from Manama?

faqs.q: Why is Ain Sokhna the fastest sea route from Dubai to Egypt?

Alexandria and Damietta sit on the Mediterranean and are reached through Suez in 14–18 days. For Cairo, Suez and the Red Sea coast, Ain Sokhna is usually both the shorter sea leg and the shorter road leg.

faqs.q: What is an ACID number and who raises it?
faqs.a: ACID is the advance cargo declaration number on the Nafeza platform. The importer raises it against the specific consignment, and we supply the exporter details and line-by-line description it needs. The invoice, packing list and shipping documents must carry the ACID number when the container is loaded, so send the importer’s details at quotation and the registration runs while the order is picked.

faqs.q: What happens if a container sails without an ACID number?
faqs.a: It is refused rather than delayed. Egypt treats advance cargo information as a condition of loading, not a formality to catch up at the port, so a consignment without the ACID number on its documents cannot simply be cleared late. That is why the registration comes before we book the container, never after, and why an Egypt order does not load until the number is confirmed.

faqs.q: Does the exporter need to be registered with GOEIC?
faqs.a: Yes. The exporter has to be registered with the General Organization for Export and Import Control for the goods concerned, and that registration sits behind the ACID process. It is done once and then extended per product scope, and we handle it from Dubai. If an order includes product lines outside our registered scope, we say so at quotation rather than discovering it at loading.

faqs.q: Which documents travel with a shipment to Egypt?
faqs.a: The invoice and packing list carrying the ACID number, a Certificate of Origin attested by Dubai Chamber, and material and test certificates where the order calls for them. The ACID number itself is raised on Nafeza by the importer, with our GOEIC registration behind it. Everything is prepared in Dubai before the container loads, so the document set matches the registration exactly.

faqs.q: Should we ship to Ain Sokhna, Alexandria or Damietta?
faqs.a: Ain Sokhna for Cairo, Suez, the Sokhna industrial zone and the Red Sea oil coast, at 8–12 days by sea. Alexandria or Damietta for the Delta, Borg El Arab, the Idku area and western deliveries, at 14–18 days through Suez. A few extra days at sea are often outweighed by a shorter inland leg, so we quote the routing that reaches your site soonest.

faqs.q: How fast can you air-freight to Cairo when a line is down?
faqs.a: Typically 3–5 days from dispatch, flown from DXB to Cairo. Air is for line-down orders: a failed hose assembly, a seal kit, a replacement valve. For planned stock it rarely pays on this lane, so we usually suggest consolidating hose, fittings and adapters into one sea shipment and keeping a spare of each critical assembly on site rather than expediting the next failure.

faqs.q: Can you deliver to the Western Desert fields and the Gulf of Suez?

Western Desert deliveries land at Alexandria or Ain Sokhna and move inland by road, while Ras Gharib and Ras Shukheir are reached down the Red Sea coast from Ain Sokhna. The inland leg is quoted rather than estimated, and site access requirements should come with the order so the truck is not turned back at the gate.

faqs.q: Can you supply to refinery and LNG specifications?
faqs.a: Yes. We supply API 6A and API 16C rated items and NACE MR0175 material for sour service, with material certificates, plus SS316L fittings and tube for process service. That covers the duty found at the refineries around Alexandria, Suez and Assiut and at the Idku and Damietta LNG plants, quoted line by line against the specification in the tender.

faqs.q: Do you deliver to 10th of Ramadan, Sadat City and Borg El Arab?

We quote the port and the road leg together on one Estimate, so the delivered terms are clear before the ACID number is raised.

faqs.q: Do you make up hose assemblies to length for Egypt?
faqs.a: Yes. Assemblies are crimped to length and pressure-tested in Dubai and shipped as finished items, tagged with the hose, the fitting and the test date.
